title: A Routine Question for Every Patient

patient.name: Mdm Aw Bee Choo
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine annual eye check, no new visual complaints

history.hpc: Mdm Aw is a 79-year-old attending for her routine annual eye check. She walks into the clinic unassisted, without any mobility aid, and reports no new visual symptoms. As part of standard registration, the PSA performs a fall risk screen for every patient regardless of presenting complaint, as required at every visit.
history.pmhx: Mild cataract both eyes (stable, monitored). Hypertension on medication. Osteoporosis diagnosed 5 years ago, on calcium and vitamin D supplements.
history.social_hx: Lives alone in a one-room flat. Independent with all activities of daily living. No history of falls in the past year. Walks to the nearby market daily.

examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed at this stage — doctor to review

fall_risk_screen.visual_impairment: No significant impairment — VA 6/9 both eyes, mild cataract only
fall_risk_screen.overall_assessment: Low risk based on screening — age is the only contributing factor present
fall_risk_screen.action_required: No additional fall prevention measures required today; document screen as completed with low-risk outcome

diagnosis: Fall risk screening completed at registration as required for every patient at every visit. Mdm Aw screens as low risk today — age over 65 is the only factor present, with no falls history, no mobility aid use, no significant visual impairment, and no sedating medications. Result documented; routine eye check to proceed.

immediate: As part of standard registration for every patient, ask Mdm Aw the fall risk screening questions regardless of the fact she presents with no mobility issues
Ask whether she has had any falls in the past year — confirm 'No'
Note whether she uses any mobility aid (cane, walker, wheelchair) — confirm she walks unassisted
Note her current vision level (VA 6/9 both eyes) and any known visual impairment affecting mobility — none significant
Review her medication list for sedating or high-risk medications (e.g., opioids, benzodiazepines, sedating antihistamines) — none identified
Calculate and document the overall fall risk outcome based on the factors present (age >65 only)
Since the result is low risk, no special fall prevention measures (e.g., wristband, escort) are required today
Document the completed fall risk screen in SCM as part of her registration record
Proceed with the routine VA and other tests for her annual check as normal
follow_up: File the completed fall risk screen with her registration documentation
Note that the screen should be repeated at her next visit, as required for every visit
No escalation to nurse-in-charge required given the low-risk outcome
patient_education: Briefly explain to Mdm Aw that fall risk screening is a routine safety check done for all patients at every visit, not because of any specific concern about her
General fall prevention advice can be offered: ensure good lighting at home, wear well-fitted footwear, and use handrails where available
Encourage her to inform staff if she ever feels unsteady or dizzy during a future visit, even if her screen was previously low risk

key_points: Performs the fall risk screen for every patient regardless of presenting complaint or apparent mobility
Asks specifically about falls history in the past year
Asks about mobility aid use and reviews the medication list for sedating/high-risk drugs
Considers visual impairment level as part of the screen, using the VA results available
Systematically goes through each fall risk domain rather than skipping the screen because the patient appears independent
Correctly identifies that age >65 is the only risk factor present for this patient
Arrives at an overall low-risk outcome based on the absence of other risk factors
Documents the screen and its outcome clearly in the patient's record
Correctly classifies the patient as low risk based on the screening criteria
Does not over- or under-estimate risk based on the patient's appearance alone
Recognises that a low-risk result still requires documentation, not just verbal acknowledgement
Understands that the screen must be repeated at every visit, not just once
Completes and documents the fall risk screen as part of routine registration
Does not apply unnecessary fall prevention measures for a low-risk patient
Provides general, non-alarming fall prevention advice appropriate for an independent elderly patient
Proceeds smoothly with the rest of the patient's routine visit without unnecessary delay
